title: Ncaa Division I Adopts Age Based 5 Year Eligibility Model That Eliminates Redshirts Waivers
report:
**Summary:**
The NCAA Division I Cabinet has approved a new age-based, 5-year eligibility model that will replace the existing model starting with incoming students in fall 2027. The new model eliminates redshirts and waivers, instead starting student-athletes' eligibility clocks at enrollment or their 19th birthday. Current student-athletes with remaining eligibility can choose which model is more beneficial for them. The change aims to simplify eligibility rules and address issues with the current system.

**Key Facts:**

1. **New Eligibility Model:** Starting in fall 2027, the NCAA will use an age-based, 5-year eligibility model that eliminates redshirts and waivers.
2. **Eligibility Clock:** Student-athletes' eligibility clocks will start when they first enroll full-time or at the beginning of the academic year following their 19th birthday, whichever comes first.
3. **Exceptions:** The new model includes exceptions for pregnancy, active-duty military service, and official religious missions, which can delay or pause a student-athlete's eligibility clock.
4. **Grandfather Clause:** Incoming students in the class of 2026 and current student-athletes with remaining eligibility can choose between the old and new models to determine their eligibility.
5. **Effective Date:** The change will take effect for incoming students enrolling full-time in college in fall 2027 or later, although some details may still be finalized at the Division I Cabinet's meeting on Wednesday.
